clue.text: Foreign office alters estimates

parts.note: to alter something is to recast it, rework its shape

explanation.surface: The Foreign Office keeps revising its budget figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Forecasts are predictions or projections, which is what estimates of future figures are.

clue.text: An aspect of service in the Ist/4th Foot

indicators.note: in places the word for service inside the picked letters of Foot
the first and fourth letters of the four-letter word Foot are its outer pair

parts.note: an ace is an unreturnable tennis service

explanation.surface: A remark about life in an infantry regiment, the 1st/4th Foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ist' is the scan's 1st. Foot has four letters, so its 1st and 4th are F and T, which take ACE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one side or feature of something, an aspect of it.

clue.text: Resentment felt by soldier on report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for soldier is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier who serves in the ranks

explanation.surface: A soldier placed on report feels bitter about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On report' looks like military discipline but signals a sound-alike: RANKER said aloud matches RANCOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated bitterness or ill will, a synonym of resentment.

clue.text: Monarch's palace torn almost asunder

indicators.note: torn asunder means ripped apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged
almost means not quite all, so the last letter of torn is dropped

explanation.surface: A royal residence is being ripped apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims torn to TOR; PALACE plus TOR are rearranged by 'asunder'. The 's of Monarch's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruling queen of Ptolemaic Egypt, a monarch.

clue.text: Force through vessel with inherent list

indicators.note: inherent means existing within, so the word for list sits inside the vessel

parts.note: a steamer is a steam-powered ship
a roll is a list of names, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: A ship with a permanent tilt pushes its way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' looks like a ship's tilt but means a register, ROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: To steamroller a proposal is to push it through by overwhelming force, crushing opposition.

clue.text: Sorry state of Society nowadays?

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era of years

explanation.surface: A lament about the poor condition of modern society.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (anno domini) labels the years of the present era, hence 'nowadays'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorry in the sense of pitiful or regrettable, as in a sad or sorry sight.

clue.text: Southern bird to approach carefully

parts.note: the teal is a small freshwater duck

explanation.surface: A bird from the south creeps up warily.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal up on something is to move towards it quietly and stealthily.

clue.text: Stone containing tin not plentiful

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the abbreviation for stone wraps the tin

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight of fourteen pounds
a can is a tin container

explanation.surface: A rock with only a trace of tin ore in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, meagre, the opposite of abundant.

clue.text: Grass in hedges, part of enclosure

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: Grass grows in the hedges that form part of a field boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across hedgES PART Of.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough Spanish and North African grass used for paper and rope.

clue.text: Characteristic ailment spreading around Tyneside

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the abbreviation for Tyneside
spreading suggests the letters of ailment are spread about and rearranged

parts.note: NE, North East, is the region of England containing Tyneside

explanation.surface: A disease is spreading across the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges the illness word to LIAMENT; 'around' wraps it round the region abbreviation. Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineament is a distinctive feature, especially of the face, a characteristic trait.

clue.text: Surrender collection of notes after study

indicators.note: after places the group of notes behind the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
C, E, D and E are musical notes, here collected into one group

explanation.surface: Giving up after studying a set of lecture notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests jottings, but here they are musical note letters A to G.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede is to yield or give up, as in conceding a point or a game.

clue.text: Clock without a movement?

parts.note: clock is slang for face, and a face without any movement shows no expression

explanation.surface: A timepiece missing its works.
explanation.walkthrough: A clock's movement is its mechanism; read clock as slang for face and the clue describes an impassive expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face is expressionless and impassive, showing no flicker of feeling.

clue.text: Military detachment not up to standard is sent back to square

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool, so T stands for square

indicators.note: sent back means the word for substandard is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: poor means of low quality, not up to standard

explanation.surface: A substandard unit is ordered back to the parade square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is sent back' turns POOR into ROOP; 'square' gives T, from the T-square used by draughtsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a cavalry or artillery unit, a small body of soldiers.

clue.text: Postponements find speaker set in intention to come back

indicators.note: set in means the speaker is placed inside the reversed word for intention
come back means the word for intention is turned around

parts.note: an aim is an intention or purpose
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: Delays occur as a lecturer is placed in a plan to return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come back' turns the intention word into MIA; 'set in' then houses the speaker inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Moratoria is the plural of moratorium, a legally authorised delay or suspension.

clue.text: Nerve shown in series of games producing inquisitive spectators

indicators.note: shown in places the word for nerve inside the series of games

parts.note: a rubber is a series of games in bridge or whist
neck is slang for cheek or audacity, nerve

explanation.surface: Displays of nerve over several card games attract nosy onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: A rubber is a match of usually three games in bridge; NECK (brazen nerve) goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubberneckers crane their necks to gawp at something, nosy onlookers.

clue.text: Musical section augmenting gong

explanation.surface: A section of music adding to the sound of a gong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' is British slang for a medal; a bar is a clasp added to a medal ribbon for a further award.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure of music is one sense; the other is a metal clasp added to a military decoration.

clue.text: Material support for sponsor of stage set piece

indicators.note: in a down entry the lower word supports the upper one, so the material sits below

parts.note: to back someone is to sponsor or support them
cloth is a woven fabric, material

explanation.surface: Fabric used to support the backer of a theatrical scenery piece.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the material sits beneath the sponsor word, which is why it is the 'support for' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A backcloth is the painted curtain hung at the back of a theatre stage as scenery.

clue.text: Foreign money in volume difficult to handle

indicators.note: in means the foreign currency goes inside the word for volume

parts.note: a tome is a large book, a volume
roubles are the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: Foreign banknotes in large quantity are awkward to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' looks like quantity but means a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Troublesome means causing difficulty or annoyance, awkward to manage.

clue.text: Directions on trip with mature attendants

parts.note: E and N are compass directions, east and north
a tour is a trip or journey
to age is to mature or grow older

explanation.surface: Guidance about a holiday with grown-up companions.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of people who accompany and attend an important person.

clue.text: Contraction of brief illness

parts.note: curt means short or brief, especially rudely so
an ailment is an illness

explanation.surface: Catching a short-lived illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtailment is a cutting short or reduction, a contraction in size or length.

clue.text: Again negotiate for shelter

explanation.surface: Renegotiating a deal for somewhere to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints '97)' where the count (7) should be.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-treat is to deal with or negotiate once more; a retreat is also a secluded refuge or place of safety.

clue.text: Tank needs very aggressive troop leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the three words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A tank requires its troop to have very aggressive commanders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tank' suggests an armoured vehicle in a military scene; it is a container for liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A vat is a large container for holding liquids, a tank.

clue.text: One habitation erected say, for the community

parts.note: a villa is a single house, one dwelling

indicators.note: erected means set upright, so in a down entry the word for say is read upwards

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: A single house is built, so to speak, for the local people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns EG into GE in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A village is a small rural settlement and the community living in it.

clue.text: Is able to harbour a river vessel

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter within, so the word for is able holds the rest

parts.note: can means is able to
the Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall

explanation.surface: A river boat can be kept in a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is a river in south-west England; 'harbour' looks nautical but means contain.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a boat with two parallel hulls, a vessel.

clue.text: Encountered gangster on the road

parts.note: met is the past tense of meet, encountered
Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: Meeting a mobster while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Road metal is the British term for the broken stone used to surface roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal, or road metal, is crushed stone laid as a roadway surface.

clue.text: One left in dark

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for left inside the word for one

parts.note: a unit is a single thing, one

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in the darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means without light, so dark.

clue.text: Set to enmesh bears

indicators.note: to enmesh is to tangle up in a net, so the letters are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting ready to trap bears in a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animals but is the verb meaning carries.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry, so totes means carries or bears.

clue.text: Surpass in openwork

parts.note: split into open and work: overt means open, not hidden
op, short for opus, is a work of music

explanation.surface: Excelling at delicate lace with patterned holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openwork' is lace with holes, but read as 'open' (OVERT) and 'work' (OP).
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to rise above or exceed, to surpass.

clue.text: Add to drink in cup

annotationWithheld.why: Add to drink in cup (3): POT may be cup (a trophy), but no sound reading of 'Add to drink' gives POT, and reversing TOP needs an indicator the clue lacks

clue.text: The French crew in court making a noise

indicators.note: in places the French article and crew inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: la is French for the, feminine
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: French sailors in a law court cause a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamant means clamorous or noisy, from the Latin for shouting.

clue.text: Lodging house permit retracted

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the word for permit is reversed

parts.note: to let is to permit or allow

explanation.surface: A licence to run a boarding house is withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retracted' turns the permit word into TEL; 'Lodging house' reads as one phrase but splits into definition and abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel provides lodging, accommodation for paying guests.

clue.text: Girl entertaining dubious tales is lacking in delicacy

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the girl's name contains the rest

parts.note: Tess is a girl's name, as in Hardy's heroine

indicators.note: dubious suggests the tales are doubtful, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl telling suspect stories shows no refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dubious' rearranges the stories into ASTEL, which 'entertaining' sets inside the girl's name, splitting it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteless means crude or vulgar, without refinement or discretion.
